workspace.placeholder: Example: Every day at 9:00, fetch open shipments from the ERP and check inventory. If stock is available, create a delivery order and notify the warehouse; otherwise alert procurement…
example_values: Every day at 9:00, fetch open shipments from the ERP and check inventory. If stock is available, notify the warehouse; otherwise alert procurement and log an exception.
Every day, collect items below safety stock and prepare replenishment suggestions. After buyer confirmation, create purchase requests and update the warehouse.
After daily reconciliation, find documents with mismatched amounts. Notify operations for review, then escalate to the finance lead if unresolved after two hours.

faq.label: FAQ
faq.title: What teams ask before deployment
faq.description: Clear answers about generated workflows, data handling, and n8n setup.

items.title: Can I import the JSON directly into n8n?
items.description: Yes. The generated nodes and connections form an importable skeleton. Your real ERP endpoints, credentials, and field mappings still need to be configured in n8n.

items.title: Do I need to know n8n first?
items.description: No. Operations teams can describe and review the SOP first, while technical owners complete connections and production validation.

items.title: Does it store ERP credentials?
items.description: The current foundation generates drafts locally in your browser and never asks you to put secrets in the SOP. Production connections should use n8n credentials.

items.title: Which ERP processes fit best?
items.description: Order fulfillment, replenishment, purchasing approvals, reconciliation, master-data sync, and exception alerts are strong starting points.

items.title: How does the AI analysis work?
items.description: ERP SOP analysis and n8n orchestration prompts are embedded in the product. This preview uses deterministic local generation; a model service can extend complex language and branch recognition next.
